title: Give the workspace-admin verdict a "not resolved yet" state instead of collapsing it into `false`
body:
Fixes #5619

`useIsWorkspaceAdmin(): boolean` had no third answer, so "the inputs have not arrived yet" and "resolved: not an admin" were the same `false`, and every gate downstream acted on it.

## Fix shape: (a), and the evidence that chose it

Triage left the shape to the implementing dev with evidence. Both named shapes were acceptable; this is (a) — widen the hook — because measurement made (b) the wrong trade.

**(b) — extend `ConnectedShell`'s gate — costs everyone and buys the protected population nothing.** The gate would have to wait for the whole organization pipeline (`listOrganizations` → `getActiveOrganization` → the ADR-0081 `setActiveOrganization` repair → `getActiveMember`), which today runs *concurrently* with the metadata tree that `ConnectedShell` mounts. Two measurements decided it:

- **On a single-tenant deployment `getActiveMember()` is never called at all.** `AuthProvider.refreshActiveMember` returns early on `!activeOrganization`, so a gate waiting for the member row to "resolve meaningfully" waits on a request that is never made. Pinned as `a single-tenant deployment resolves without ever asking for a member row`.
- **The admins this card protects mostly do not need the wait.** framework `plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` builds `positions[]` in `customSession`, and its org leg reads `session.activeOrganizationId` — `if (!orgId) return []`. When the session *was* minted with an active organization stamped, the member row is already in `positions` as `org_owner`/`org_admin`, and leg 3 answers on the first frame. Gating the shell would make those admins wait for an answer they already have.

**(a) puts the wait exactly where the answer is missing.** `isResolved` is true the instant `isAdmin` is, so any admin the session already identifies pays zero extra frames — pinned as `an admin the session already identifies is resolved on the first frame, with the pipeline still open`, which asserts the verdict while the org pipeline is deliberately left hanging.

(a) also survives what (b) cannot: `MarketplacePage`, `HomePage` and the chrome are all published exports of `@object-ui/app-shell`, mountable by a consumer with no `ConnectedShell` above them.

## Root coverage, not per-page masks

Triage's binding constraint was that the fix cover both consequence shapes at the root, and not reintroduce the kind of mask #5621 correctly removed. Two shared mount points and the two published refusal surfaces:

| Where | Covers |
|---|---|
| `AppContent`'s existing readiness gate (one clause) | the redirect below it, the chrome (`ConsoleLayout` → `UnifiedSidebar`, `AppHeader`), the four views, `InstalledListWidget`, both marketplace routes, `SystemHubPage` |
| `HomePage`'s existing metadata gate (one clause) | the one admin-gated route outside `AppContent` |
| `MarketplacePage` / `MarketplacePackagePage` guard stacks | the severe consequence, at surfaces a consumer can mount alone |

Neither addition is a mask: both are the *existing* readiness gate of the surface, and the admin verdict is demonstrably one of its inputs. The `!marketplaceEnabled` ordering established by #5557 / #5533 is untouched and pinned.

## A third consequence shape, not in the report or the grading

`AppContent` guards the zero-app strand with `!activeApp && … && !isWorkspaceAdmin` and answers with a `Navigate to="/home" replace`. That is not a repaint — a repaint corrects itself when the verdict flips; a replace-navigation does not, and the strand is erased from history behind the administrator. Metadata and the org pipeline race, and the org pipeline is the longer of the two, so the branch was reached with the verdict still in flight. Covered by the same gate.

## Breaking change

`useIsWorkspaceAdmin` is **removed**, not kept alongside `useWorkspaceAdminStatus`. A caller that ignores the third state is the entire defect, and keeping the boolean means the next reader reintroduces it silently. Removing it makes a missed call site a compile error. `minor` per this repo's version policy (never `major` in the fixed group).

`AuthProvider` gains `isMembershipResolved` on its context. This was unavoidable: `organizations` / `activeOrganization` / `activeMember` read `[]` / `null` / `null` both before the pipeline starts and after it finds nothing, and `isOrganizationsLoading` is `false` on both sides of the request — no combination of existing fields distinguishes "not asked yet" from "asked, and there is none". It is derived from two internal *positive* resolution flags rather than another `isLoading`, and closes on every path including both failure paths, so no gate can hang on it.

## Verification

A render-ordering fix is invisible to a type-check, so every claim above is asserted from a real mount, as a **pair of frames** — unresolved, then resolved.

- `packages/auth/src/__tests__/workspaceAdminUnresolved-5619.test.tsx` drives the real `AuthProvider` against a client double whose promises are held open by hand, so each step of the pipeline is a separate observable frame.
- `MarketplaceRefusalResolution-5619.test.tsx` and `AppContent.unresolvedAdmin-5619.test.tsx` mount the real surfaces and read the frame before and after resolution.

Negatives are pinned alongside every positive, in the discipline #5389 established on this hook: a settled non-admin is still refused, a settled non-admin with no accessible app still bounces, the runtime-off answer still comes first, and nobody new becomes an admin. A fix that simply stopped refusing, or that held the resolving frame forever, fails those.

**Reverse-verified.** Collapsing `isResolved` back to always-true and removing the three surface gates turns all three new files red — 8 tests, in the predicted direction — and the negatives above stay green. Mutations were confirmed on disk by before/after counts of the exact replaced text plus the injected marker, and restored under an `EXIT` trap.

Green at `b418d910a`: `turbo run type-check` for `@object-ui/auth` + `@object-ui/app-shell` + `@object-ui/console` — 38/38 tasks. Vitest over the derived superset — 502 test files, 4676 tests, 1 skipped, no failures.
